ann_24.text: This part of the model, which reads a3 and a6, barely changes the predictions.

ann_25.text: This part of the model, which reads only a3, barely changes the predictions.

ann_26.text: This part reads only a3; through it, changing a3 from 1 to 2 clearly lowers the typical case's predicted probability of 'yes' from about 72% to about 10%.
In the model as a whole the same change clearly raises it to above 99%, so other parts outweigh this one.

ann_27.text: This part of the model acts on the 168 training cases with a3 = 2, and 60 of them are actually 'yes'.
For the typical case it acts on (a1 = 1, a2 = 1, a3 = 2, a4 = 2, a5 = 4, a6 = 1), it clearly raises the predicted probability of 'yes' from below 1% without the part to above 99% with it.
Through this part, changing a3 from 1 to 2 clearly raises the typical case's predicted probability of 'yes' from about 72% to above 99%.
The effect of that change clearly depends on a1: for the typical case with a1 other than 3 it goes from about 72% to above 99%, while with a1 = 3 it is above 99% either way.
For the typical case it acts on, a1 = 3 slightly raises the predicted probability of 'yes', which is above 99% either way (on the training data only).

ann_28.text: Through this part, changing a3 from 1 to 2 clearly lowers the typical case's predicted probability of 'yes' from about 72% to about 2%.
Changing a6 from 1 to 2 raises it to about 99% (on the training data only).

ann_29.text: Through this part, giving a2 or a4 its first value clearly lowers the typical case's predicted probability of 'yes' from about 72% to below 1%, and changing a2 from 3 to 2 clearly lowers it to about 12%.
Moving a1, a5 or a6 away from its first value through this part clearly raises it to above 99%.
Changing a3 from 1 to 2 through this part clearly lowers it to about 1%, the opposite of what the same change does in the model as a whole, where it clearly raises it to above 99%.

ann_30.text: Through this part, changing a3 from 1 to 2 clearly raises the typical case's predicted probability of 'yes' from about 72% to above 99%.
Changing a6 from 1 to 2 raises it to about 99% (on the training data only).
Giving a1 the value 3 slightly raises it, leaving it at about 72% (on the training data only).

ann_31.text: For the typical case, the model gives a predicted probability of 'yes' of about 72%.
Giving a2 or a4 its first value clearly lowers it to below 1%, and changing a2 from 3 to 2 clearly lowers it to about 12%.
Moving a1, a3, a5 or a6 away from its first value clearly raises it to above 99%.

ann_24.original: Dead unit 1083 = ReLU(0.298 z(a3:1) + 1.13 z(a6:2) - 1.95). Analytically the maximum pre-activation over the whole input domain is -0.502 (a3=1, a6=2), so the unit is identically zero on all 432 configurations. Empirically (train, n=345, full sample) its output distribution is min=max=0. It reads a3 and a6, but contributes nothing to the gate (0.284) or the relay (-1.324).
ann_24.proposed: This part barely changes the predictions.

ann_25.original: Dead unit 2445 = ReLU(0.706 z(a3:1) - 1.49). Maximum pre-activation -0.802 < 0 over the input domain, so it is identically zero; train output distribution (n=345) min=max=0. Its -0.109 readout into the output contributes nothing.
ann_25.proposed: This part barely changes the predictions.

ann_26.original: Always-on a3 offset: 639 = ReLU(2.16 z(a3:2) + 3.14) takes exactly two values, 1.04 (a3=1) and 5.36 (a3=2), never clipped (train n=345: min 1.04, max 5.36). Through its -0.721 readout it adds -0.75 (a3=1) or -3.86 (a3=2) to the logit: a linear a3 term of -3.11 for a3=2.
ann_26.proposed: This part lowers the predicted probability of 'yes' when a3 changes from 1 to 2, against the direction of the model as a whole.

ann_27.original: a3=2 gate with a1=3 modulation: 435 = ReLU(0.317 z(a1:3) + 6.72 z(a3:2) + 0.284*h1083 - 3.36), h1083 = 0. Analytically: a3=1 gives pre-activation -10.12 / -9.44 (off); a3=2 gives 3.33 (a1 in {1,2}) or 4.01 (a1=3). Train (n=345): output in {0, 3.33, 4.01}, mean 1.71, median 0, two regimes (regime_map), on for 48.7% of rows (= the a3=2 rows). This is the network's only active nonlinearity; it acts as an a3 indicator (a3=2 -> on) plus the network's only interaction (a1=3 & a3=2 adds 0.685 to the gate, i.e. +7.33 to the logit after the gate's total gain of 10.70).
ann_27.proposed: This part acts on the cases with a3 = 2 and raises their predicted probability of 'yes'; how much the a3 change matters depends on whether a1 = 3.

ann_28.original: Linear relay: 821 = ReLU(5.77 - 0.893 z(a3:2) + 0.627 z(a6:2) + id), id = 2.542*h435 - 1.324*h1083 >= 0; 1957 = ReLU(1.63*h821 + 1.71). Over all 432 inputs 821 pre-activation ranges 6.03..15.70 and 1957 11.55..27.35: neither ReLU ever clips, so the pair is exactly linear on the domain. Train (n=345) output distribution: 821 in [6.03, 15.70]. Combined with the readouts (-0.673 on 821, 2.148 on 1957) the relay multiplies its input by 2.837 on the logit: gate x 7.21, a6=2 -> +3.56, a3=2 -> -5.07 relative to a3=1.
ann_28.proposed: This part lowers the predicted probability of 'yes' when a3 changes from 1 to 2 and, on the training data only, raises it when a6 changes from 1 to 2.

ann_29.original: Linear count of first-value indicators, read through nine direct edges (exact linear, no nonlinearity). Per-attribute logit contributions (first value vs others): a1 -12.43 vs +6.80; a2 -15.91 vs +6.55 (a2=2) / +9.48 (a2=3); a4 -12.09 vs +5.44; a5 -16.11 vs +8.18 (a5=2) / +4.04 (a5=3,4); a6 -9.18 vs +9.68. Each of these indicators lowers the logit by 17.5..24.3. a3 has the opposite (small) sign directly: a3=1 +2.56 vs a3=2 -2.70; the a3_pathway reverses this. Train (n=345): id_linear ranges -68.4..42.1 (mean 0, sd 21.5), and per indicator count k its range is k=0: 29.8..36.9, k=2: -12.8..24.6, k=4: -50.9..-13.5, k=6: -63.2.
ann_29.proposed: This part lowers the predicted probability of 'yes' when a2 or a4 takes its first value (and when a2 is 2 rather than 3) and raises it when a1, a5 or a6 moves away from its first value; its a3 effect runs the other way to the model as a whole.

ann_30.original: The hidden pathway (children: dead_a3a6_unit_1083, dead_a3_unit_2445, a3_offset_639, a3_gate_435, linear_relay_821_1957). id_hidden = 3.489*h435 - 0.721*h639 - 0.673*h821 + 2.148*h1957 - 0.109*h2445; the relay is fed by 2.542*h435 - 1.324*h1083 and the gate by 0.284*h1083; both dead units are 0, and the relay and offset are linear on the domain, so the only nonlinearity is the a3 gate, which reaches the output with total gain 3.489 + 2.542*2.837 = 10.70. Result: a lookup on (a3, a6, a1=3): +20.01 (a3=1,a6=1), +23.57 (a3=1,a6=2), +47.44 (a3=2,a6=1), +51.00 (a3=2,a6=2), plus +7.33 when a3=2 and a1=3. Train (n=345): id_hidden takes exactly these six values (min 20.01, max 58.33). Function: it supplies the a3 'first value' indicator (a3=1 lowers the logit by 27.4, or 34.8 if a1=3; net -22.2 / -29.5 after the linear part's +5.25) and adds a small a6 term (a6=1 lowers by a further 3.56, total a6 drop 22.4).
ann_30.proposed: This part raises the predicted probability of 'yes' when a3 changes from 1 to 2, and, on the training data only, when a6 changes from 1 to 2.

ann_31.original: Root: output = sigmoid(1.208 + Linear + A3Pathway), an additive composition of linear_count_down and a3_pathway under the output sigmoid. Unconnected inputs a1:2, a4:2, a4:3, a5:3, a5:4, a6:1 are zero-effect entries (their one-hot siblings carry the same information). Net: logit ~ 80 - 20*k, where k = number of attributes taking their first value; per-indicator drops a1 19.2, a2 22.5/25.4, a3 22.2 (29.5 if a1=3), a4 17.5, a5 24.3/20.1, a6 22.4. Exhaustive check over all 432 configurations: logit 82..96 (k=0), 60..79 (k=1), 37..56 (k=2), 15..32 (k=3), -5.2..7.7 (k=4, 49% positive, depending on which attributes are first-valued: the a1/a4 indicators drop the least), <-16 (k>=5). The decision equals 'k <= 3' on 94.4% of the 432 configurations (all disagreements at k=4). The model is a saturated monotone 'at most three (sometimes four) first values' detector. Train (n=345): output median 1.0, mean 0.915; accuracy 0.41, AUC 0.81. Compared with the target rule (exactly two first values) it agrees on 41.4% of the 432 configurations: it learned only the upper edge of the k=2 peak (k>=4/5 -> negative), placed one step too high, and has no lower edge (k=0,1 -> positive).
ann_31.proposed: For the typical case (about 72% 'yes'), giving a2 or a4 its first value clearly takes the model to 'no', and moving a1, a3, a5 or a6 away from its first value clearly takes it to 'yes'; a2 = 2 and a2 = 3 are treated differently.

summary.text: For the typical case (the most common value of each attribute: a1 = 1, a2 = 3, a3 = 1, a4 = 2, a5 = 1, a6 = 1), the model gives a predicted probability of 'yes' of about 72%.
Giving a2 or a4 its first value clearly lowers it to below 1%, and changing a2 from 3 to 2 clearly lowers it to about 12%.
Moving a1, a3, a5 or a6 away from its first value clearly raises it to above 99%.
Changing a3 from 1 to 2 clearly raises the predicted probability of 'yes' from about 72% to above 99% for the typical case with a1 other than 3, while with a1 = 3 it is above 99% either way.
Two small parts of the model barely change the predictions.

worth_checking.flag: model does not follow the exactly-two rule
worth_checking.text: Worth checking: the typical case has four attributes at their first value (a1, a3, a5 and a6) and gets a predicted probability of 'yes' of about 72%, and moving any one of them away from its first value, which leaves three, clearly raises it to above 99%, while the exactly-two rule counts both four and three as 'no'.

worth_checking.flag: attribute values other than the first matter
worth_checking.text: Worth checking: the model clearly separates two values of a2 other than the first: for the typical case, a2 = 2 gives a predicted probability of 'yes' of about 12% and a2 = 3 about 72%.

parts.original_hypothesis: Root: output = sigmoid(1.208 + Linear + A3Pathway), an additive composition of linear_count_down and a3_pathway under the output sigmoid. Unconnected inputs a1:2, a4:2, a4:3, a5:3, a5:4, a6:1 are zero-effect entries (their one-hot siblings carry the same information). Net: logit ~ 80 - 20*k, where k = number of attributes taking their first value; per-indicator drops a1 19.2, a2 22.5/25.4, a3 22.2 (29.5 if a1=3), a4 17.5, a5 24.3/20.1, a6 22.4. Exhaustive check over all 432 configurations: logit 82..96 (k=0), 60..79 (k=1), 37..56 (k=2), 15..32 (k=3), -5.2..7.7 (k=4, 49% positive, depending on which attributes are first-valued: the a1/a4 indicators drop the least), <-16 (k>=5). The decision equals 'k <= 3' on 94.4% of the 432 configurations (all disagreements at k=4). The model is a saturated monotone 'at most three (sometimes four) first values' detector. Train (n=345): output median 1.0, mean 0.915; accuracy 0.41, AUC 0.81. Compared with the target rule (exactly two first values) it agrees on 41.4% of the 432 configurations: it learned only the upper edge of the k=2 peak (k>=4/5 -> negative), placed one step too high, and has no lower edge (k=0,1 -> positive).

parts.name: linear_count_down
parts.original_hypothesis: Linear count of first-value indicators, read through nine direct edges (exact linear, no nonlinearity). Per-attribute logit contributions (first value vs others): a1 -12.43 vs +6.80; a2 -15.91 vs +6.55 (a2=2) / +9.48 (a2=3); a4 -12.09 vs +5.44; a5 -16.11 vs +8.18 (a5=2) / +4.04 (a5=3,4); a6 -9.18 vs +9.68. Each of these indicators lowers the logit by 17.5..24.3. a3 has the opposite (small) sign directly: a3=1 +2.56 vs a3=2 -2.70; the a3_pathway reverses this. Train (n=345): id_linear ranges -68.4..42.1 (mean 0, sd 21.5), and per indicator count k its range is k=0: 29.8..36.9, k=2: -12.8..24.6, k=4: -50.9..-13.5, k=6: -63.2.

parts.name: a3_gate_435
parts.original_hypothesis: a3=2 gate with a1=3 modulation: 435 = ReLU(0.317 z(a1:3) + 6.72 z(a3:2) + 0.284*h1083 - 3.36), h1083 = 0. Analytically: a3=1 gives pre-activation -10.12 / -9.44 (off); a3=2 gives 3.33 (a1 in {1,2}) or 4.01 (a1=3). Train (n=345): output in {0, 3.33, 4.01}, mean 1.71, median 0, two regimes (regime_map), on for 48.7% of rows (= the a3=2 rows). This is the network's only active nonlinearity; it acts as an a3 indicator (a3=2 -> on) plus the network's only interaction (a1=3 & a3=2 adds 0.685 to the gate, i.e. +7.33 to the logit after the gate's total gain of 10.70).

parts.name: a3_pathway
parts.original_hypothesis: The hidden pathway (children: dead_a3a6_unit_1083, dead_a3_unit_2445, a3_offset_639, a3_gate_435, linear_relay_821_1957). id_hidden = 3.489*h435 - 0.721*h639 - 0.673*h821 + 2.148*h1957 - 0.109*h2445; the relay is fed by 2.542*h435 - 1.324*h1083 and the gate by 0.284*h1083; both dead units are 0, and the relay and offset are linear on the domain, so the only nonlinearity is the a3 gate, which reaches the output with total gain 3.489 + 2.542*2.837 = 10.70. Result: a lookup on (a3, a6, a1=3): +20.01 (a3=1,a6=1), +23.57 (a3=1,a6=2), +47.44 (a3=2,a6=1), +51.00 (a3=2,a6=2), plus +7.33 when a3=2 and a1=3. Train (n=345): id_hidden takes exactly these six values (min 20.01, max 58.33). Function: it supplies the a3 'first value' indicator (a3=1 lowers the logit by 27.4, or 34.8 if a1=3; net -22.2 / -29.5 after the linear part's +5.25) and adds a small a6 term (a6=1 lowers by a further 3.56, total a6 drop 22.4).

parts.name: linear_relay_821_1957
parts.original_hypothesis: Linear relay: 821 = ReLU(5.77 - 0.893 z(a3:2) + 0.627 z(a6:2) + id), id = 2.542*h435 - 1.324*h1083 >= 0; 1957 = ReLU(1.63*h821 + 1.71). Over all 432 inputs 821 pre-activation ranges 6.03..15.70 and 1957 11.55..27.35: neither ReLU ever clips, so the pair is exactly linear on the domain. Train (n=345) output distribution: 821 in [6.03, 15.70]. Combined with the readouts (-0.673 on 821, 2.148 on 1957) the relay multiplies its input by 2.837 on the logit: gate x 7.21, a6=2 -> +3.56, a3=2 -> -5.07 relative to a3=1.

parts.name: a3_offset_639
parts.original_hypothesis: Always-on a3 offset: 639 = ReLU(2.16 z(a3:2) + 3.14) takes exactly two values, 1.04 (a3=1) and 5.36 (a3=2), never clipped (train n=345: min 1.04, max 5.36). Through its -0.721 readout it adds -0.75 (a3=1) or -3.86 (a3=2) to the logit: a linear a3 term of -3.11 for a3=2.

parts.name: dead_a3a6_unit_1083
parts.original_hypothesis: Dead unit 1083 = ReLU(0.298 z(a3:1) + 1.13 z(a6:2) - 1.95). Analytically the maximum pre-activation over the whole input domain is -0.502 (a3=1, a6=2), so the unit is identically zero on all 432 configurations. Empirically (train, n=345, full sample) its output distribution is min=max=0. It reads a3 and a6, but contributes nothing to the gate (0.284) or the relay (-1.324).

parts.name: dead_a3_unit_2445
parts.original_hypothesis: Dead unit 2445 = ReLU(0.706 z(a3:1) - 1.49). Maximum pre-activation -0.802 < 0 over the input domain, so it is identically zero; train output distribution (n=345) min=max=0. Its -0.109 readout into the output contributes nothing.

reference_patient.definition: the typical patient: the median training patient for every number and the most common training category for every category (not a real patient)

confidence_rules.clearly: a meaningful change in predicted risk for a typical patient (at least 5% points), the test split agrees (same sign, and its bootstrap interval over test patients excludes no benefit), and every group has at least 20 training patients
confidence_rules.consistently across patients: the claim holds for at least 90% of training patients (range across patients); this is not a significance statement
confidence_rules.on the training data only: the test split disagrees (opposite sign, or no benefit on test patients) or is unclear (its interval includes no benefit), or no test check is available
confidence_rules.slightly: the change in predicted risk for a typical patient is below 5% points
confidence_rules.the model has little data on this: a compared group has fewer than 20 training patients

settings.effect_scale: log-odds (output pre-activation) for verification; predicted risk for the typical patient for wording
